description: Run one or more SQL statements against any registered resource exposing .get_connection() -- one component covering postgres/mysql/duckdb/databricks_sql/mssql/oracle/db2/doris/starburst/starrocks/timescaledb/trino instead of a dialect-specific asset per resource type.

resource_key.description: Key of a registered resource that exposes .get_connection() returning a DBAPI connection (directly, or via its own @contextmanager). Matches postgres_resource, mysql_resource, duckdb_resource, databricks_sql_resource, mssql_resource, oracle_resource, db2_resource, doris_resource, starburst_resource, starrocks_resource, timescaledb_resource, trino_resource. For Snowflake, use snowflake_sql_asset instead. Set exactly one of resource_key / connection_env (unless dry_run is True). Using resource_key means this asset's definitions require that resource to be registered to load at all (dg check defs / dg dev fail otherwise) -- a real, unavoidable Dagster constraint. Use connection_env or dry_run instead if you need this asset to load before the resource is wired up.
resource_key.label: Resource Key

sql.description: SQL text, run in a single cursor.execute() call unless split_statements is set. Whether multiple ;-separated statements run in one call is otherwise driver-dependent (works for psycopg2/duckdb; most other drivers run only the first). Set exactly one of sql / sql_file / sql_statements.
sql.label: Sql

sql_statements.label: Sql Statements
sql_statements.description: Explicit list of statements, each run as its own cursor.execute() call -- the one way to run multiple statements that works regardless of driver. Set exactly one of sql / sql_file / sql_statements.

sql_file.label: Sql File
sql_file.description: Path (relative to the Dagster process working directory) to a .sql file, read and treated the same as `sql`. Set exactly one of sql / sql_file / sql_statements.

split_statements.label: Split Statements
split_statements.description: Only applies to sql/sql_file (a single string, possibly containing several semicolon-separated statements). When True, splits it into individual statements with sqlparse.split() (string-literal/comment aware, unlike a naive ';'.split()) and runs each as its own cursor.execute() call -- the same guaranteed-multi-statement behavior sql_statements already has, without writing it as a list. Requires the sqlparse package; raises a clear error at materialization time if it isn't installed. Invalid together with sql_statements (already a list of statements).

parameters.label: Parameters
parameters.description: Bind parameters applied to every statement -- a dict for named placeholders, or a list/tuple for positional ones. Placeholder style is whatever the underlying driver's DBAPI paramstyle is (e.g. pyformat %(name)s for psycopg2/mysql-connector, qmark ? or named :name for pyodbc/oracledb, positional %s for psycopg2) -- passed through as-is, not translated.

pre_sql.label: Pre Sql
pre_sql.description: Dialect-specific statements run before the main SQL, e.g. ['SET search_path TO analytics'] (Postgres) or ['USE mydb'] (MySQL) -- write whatever your dialect needs; this component doesn't guess it for you.

commit_per_statement.label: Commit Per Statement
commit_per_statement.description: Commit after EACH statement (pre_sql and main) instead of once at the end. Use this if a later statement's failure shouldn't roll back earlier statements that already committed (the default, single final commit, treats the whole run as one transaction on drivers that support it).

fetch_last_statement_rows.label: Fetch Last Statement Rows
fetch_last_statement_rows.description: If the LAST statement run returns rows (cursor.description is not None after it -- e.g. a closing SELECT after some setup/DDL statements), fetch them with cursor.fetchall() and include them in this asset's metadata as last_statement_rows (capped at 1000 rows). Off by default, since calling fetchall() on a cursor that never returned rows is itself driver-dependent in how it behaves.

deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).
deps.label: Deps

owners.description: Asset owners — team names (team:analytics) or email addresses.
owners.label: Owners

asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.
asset_tags.label: Asset Tags

kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.
kinds.label: Kinds

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

pool.label: Pool
pool.description: Dagster's native named concurrency pool (e.g. Airflow's `pool` -- a fixed number of slots shared across every asset/op using the same pool name, e.g. warehouse concurrency limits). The pool's own slot count is configured at the deployment level (dagster.yaml's concurrency: pools:, or the Dagster+ UI), not here.

timeout_seconds.label: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: Kill the wait and fail the run if the SQL hasn't finished after this many seconds. Enforced via a background-thread wrapper -- the underlying query may continue running past the deadline (Python threads can't be forcibly killed, and this does not cancel the query server-side); this bounds the step's wait, not the call itself.

run_window.label: Run Window
run_window.description: 'HH:MM-HH:MM tz [day,day,...]' (e.g. '09:00-17:00 America/New_York mon,tue,wed,thu,fri'). Outside this window, the asset SKIPS cleanly instead of running or failing -- no SQL runs, and real downstream dependents skip too (not fail). Checked once per materialization, before any statement runs. A malformed spec fails open (never blocks). Unset (default): always runs.

connection_env.label: Connection Env
connection_env.description: Env var holding a SQLAlchemy connection URL (e.g. 'postgresql://user:pass@host/db'), read at RUN time and connected via sqlalchemy.create_engine(url).raw_connection() -- a plain DBAPI connection, same shape resource_key's own .get_connection() returns. Unlike resource_key, this never touches Dagster's resource system at all, so this asset's definitions always load cleanly regardless of whether the env var is set yet; a missing/empty env var only fails at materialization time, with a clear message. Set exactly one of resource_key / connection_env (unless dry_run is True, which needs neither).

dry_run.label: Dry Run
dry_run.description: Log the fully-resolved SQL (pre_sql + the main statement(s)) and skip actually running it -- no resource is looked up, no SQLAlchemy engine is created, no connection is opened at all. Output metadata always includes dry_run so a materialization history shows which runs were real.
